chunks.heading: UEFIabc Context Repository
chunks.text:
This repository is the **central context store** for the UEFIabc project ecosystem.

It does not contain runnable code. Its purpose is to hold structured knowledge — decisions, conventions, project state, and conversation history — that AI assistants use when generating, reviewing, or evolving other UEFIabc projects.

Think of it as the long-term memory and source of truth for the ecosystem.

---

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Context Repository › Directory Structure
chunks.text:
| Folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`/projects`](./projects/) | One file per project: goals, status, key decisions, and links |
| [`/conversations`](./conversations/) | Saved AI conversation logs that produced important decisions or artifacts |
| [`/docs`](./docs/) | Conventions, architecture patterns, glossary, and guidelines shared across projects |
| [`/prompts`](./prompts/) | Reusable prompts and system instructions for AI work on UEFIabc projects |
| [`/decisions`](./decisions/) | Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) — what was decided, why, and what was rejected |
| [`/context-snapshots`](./context-snapshots/) | Point-in-time snapshots of ecosystem state, used to brief AI at the start of a session |

---

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Context Repository › How to Use
chunks.text:
When starting an AI-assisted session on any UEFIabc project:

1. Point the AI at the relevant `/projects/<project>.md` file.
2. Include any applicable `/docs/` conventions.
3. Pull in the latest `/context-snapshots/` if a broad overview is needed.
4. Attach relevant `/decisions/` ADRs if the work touches established architectural choices.

---

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Context Repository › What "UEFIabc" means
chunks.text: UEFIabc is the umbrella name for a collection of personal/experimental projects. The name is intentionally abstract — it is not related to UEFI firmware.

chunks.heading: ADR 001 — Create uefi-context as a Shared Context Repository › Context
chunks.text:
**Date:** 08-04-2026
**Status:** Accepted

---

The UEFIabc ecosystem will consist of multiple separate projects. AI assistants are used heavily during development. Without a shared context store, each new AI session starts from scratch — no memory of past decisions, no shared conventions, no awareness of what other projects exist or how they relate.

The risk is inconsistency: different projects making conflicting choices, AI producing output that ignores established patterns, and no single place to look up "how do we do X here."

chunks.heading: ADR 001 — Create uefi-context as a Shared Context Repository › Decision
chunks.text:
Create a dedicated repository, `uefi-context`, that holds no runnable code but acts as the **long-term memory** of the ecosystem.

It stores:
- Per-project context files (goals, status, key decisions)
- Cross-project conventions and guidelines
- Architectural Decision Records (this folder)
- Saved AI conversations that led to important outcomes
- Reusable prompts and system instructions
- Periodic ecosystem snapshots for quick AI briefing

chunks.heading: ADR 001 — Create uefi-context as a Shared Context Repository › Rationale
chunks.text:
- A single repo is easy to point AI at: "read this before we start"
- Keeping context separate from code avoids polluting individual project repos
- ADRs create a trail of *why* things are the way they are, not just *what* they are
- The cost (one extra repo to maintain) is low; the benefit compounds over time

chunks.heading: ADR 001 — Create uefi-context as a Shared Context Repository › Rejected Alternatives
chunks.text:
- **README files in each project repo** — scattered, hard to get a cross-project view, no single briefing point
- **A Notion/wiki** — external dependency, harder to version-control, not easily fed to an AI as raw files
- **No documentation** — the status quo; leads to context loss and repeated decisions

chunks.heading: ADR 001 — Create uefi-context as a Shared Context Repository › Consequences
chunks.text:
- Every new UEFIabc project gets a corresponding file in `/projects/`
- Any significant cross-project decision gets an ADR here
- AI sessions on any project should open with the relevant context files from this repo

chunks.heading: ADR 002 — One MCP Server Per Subject, With a Shared Template › Context
chunks.text:
**Date:** 08-04-2026
**Status:** Accepted

---

UFABC organizes education into a two-tier structure:
- **Courses** (e.g. Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia)
- **Subjects** (e.g. Pré-Cálculo, Circuitos Digitais)

The goal is to give Claude deep, grounded knowledge of specific subjects so it can teach, solve exercises, and reason practically about subject matter — not just answer general questions.

The question is: how to scope and package that knowledge for AI use?

chunks.heading: ADR 002 — One MCP Server Per Subject, With a Shared Template › Decision
chunks.text:
- One **MCP server per subject**, each loaded with that subject's educational content.
- One **shared template repo** (`uefi-uefimcp`) that all subject MCPs derive from.
- An optional intermediate **course-level repo** for content shared across a course's subjects (e.g. common notation, shared bibliography).

The three-level hierarchy is:

```
uefi-uefimcp ← generic template
 └── uefi-<course> ← course-level (optional aggregation layer)
 └── uefi-<subject> ← subject-level MCP (the primary unit)
```

Naming follows the pattern: `uefi-<slug>` throughout.

chunks.heading: ADR 002 — One MCP Server Per Subject, With a Shared Template › Rationale
chunks.text:
**Why one MCP per subject (not one giant MCP)?**
- A focused server can be fully loaded into context without noise from unrelated subjects
- Each subject has its own content lifecycle (exams, syllabi update each year)
- Claude performs better when the tool-space is narrow and relevant

**Why a shared template?**
- All subjects share the same core tools (syllabus, exercises, search, teach, solve)
- A template prevents drift: every subject MCP has the same structure, making them easy to maintain
- Subject-specific needs (circuit diagrams, symbolic math) are handled via feature flags in `config/subject.json`

**Why Python + `mcp` SDK?**
- Python is the natural language for academic/scientific tooling
- Optional `[math]` extras (`sympy`, `numpy`) are trivially added for quantitative subjects
- The `mcp` SDK is the reference implementation; stdio transport works with Claude Desktop and Claude Code with no configuration friction

chunks.heading: ADR 002 — One MCP Server Per Subject, With a Shared Template › Rejected Alternatives
chunks.text:
- **One giant MCP with all subjects** — too noisy; unrelated content degrades relevance of searches and tool calls
- **RAG/vector database** — adds infrastructure complexity; full-text search is sufficient at this content scale
- **TypeScript** — would require a separate optional math library story; Python's ecosystem is more naturally aligned with academic subjects

chunks.heading: ADR 002 — One MCP Server Per Subject, With a Shared Template › Consequences
chunks.text:
- Every new subject = new repo (`uefi-<subject>`) forked from `uefi-uefimcp`
- Template changes that should propagate must be manually cherry-picked into existing subject repos (no inheritance mechanism)
- The `config/subject.json` feature flag system must be kept up to date as new capabilities are added to the template
- Each subject repo must have a corresponding project file in `uefi-context/projects/`

chunks.heading: ADR 003 — uefi-prompts as Library + Generator, Not Separate Repos › Context
chunks.text:
**Date:** 08-04-2026
**Status:** Accepted

---

Prompts are first-class artifacts in the UEFIabc ecosystem. The UFABC subject MCPs use structured prompts internally (system prompt, teaching prompt, solver prompt). Beyond that, there is a broader need for a general-purpose prompt collection covering any domain — coding, creative writing, productivity, etc.

The question is: how to organize and evolve this collection?

chunks.heading: ADR 003 — uefi-prompts as Library + Generator, Not Separate Repos › Decision
chunks.text:
A single repo, `uefi-prompts`, serves both as:
1. A **static library** of Markdown prompt files organized by category
2. An **active MCP server** that can generate, rate, and improve prompts on demand

Generated and improved prompts land in the same library, distinguished by `--ai` in their filename. The library grows over time through both manual curation and AI generation.

chunks.heading: ADR 003 — uefi-prompts as Library + Generator, Not Separate Repos › Rationale
chunks.text:
**Why combine library and generator in one repo?**
- The output of the generator (new prompt files) naturally belongs in the library — there is no useful separation
- A single repo means one place to browse, search, and maintain prompts
- The MCP server is small and does not compete with the library for attention

**Why the `--ai` filename marker?**
- Origin is immediately visible in any file listing without opening the file
- `--` is visually distinct from regular hyphens in kebab-case; unlikely to appear in natural prompt names
- Greppable: `ls library/**/*--ai.md` instantly lists all AI-generated prompts
- Does not require tooling — it is just a naming convention

**Why Markdown + YAML frontmatter (not a database)?**
- Version-controlled, diffable, human-readable
- No infrastructure dependency
- Can be indexed and searched at runtime with simple file I/O
- `python-frontmatter` handles parsing without overhead

chunks.heading: ADR 003 — uefi-prompts as Library + Generator, Not Separate Repos › Rationale
chunks.text:
Version-controlled, diffable, human-readable
- No infrastructure dependency
- Can be indexed and searched at runtime with simple file I/O
- `python-frontmatter` handles parsing without overhead

**Why not embed this in `uefi-uefimcp`?**
- `uefi-prompts` is not subject-specific; it is a general tool
- The subject MCPs already have their own `/prompts/` folders for subject-specific prompt fragments
- Keeping them separate prevents scope creep in the template

chunks.heading: ADR 003 — uefi-prompts as Library + Generator, Not Separate Repos › Rejected alternatives
chunks.text:
- **Separate `uefi-prompt-library` and `uefi-prompt-generator` repos** — artificial split; the generator's only output is library files
- **A database (SQLite, JSON)** — adds tooling friction; Markdown files are simpler and version-control better
- **Numbering AI versions** — `--ai-v2` naming was chosen over `--ai-2` for readability

chunks.heading: ADR 003 — uefi-prompts as Library + Generator, Not Separate Repos › Consequences
chunks.text:
- Every prompt, regardless of origin, ends up as a `.md` file in `library/<category>/`
- The `--ai` suffix is permanent; it is not removed even if a generated prompt is later heavily edited by hand (use a manual rename if needed)
- Meta-prompts in `meta-prompts/` control the quality of generation, rating, and improvement — they should be tuned as the library grows and patterns emerge
- `uefi-context/projects/uefi-prompts.md` must be kept current as new categories or tools are added

chunks.heading: ADR 004 — uefi-mcpgen as a Dedicated Meta-Tool › Context
chunks.text:
**Date:** 08-04-2026
**Status:** Accepted

---

As the UEFIabc ecosystem grows, new MCP servers and skills will be created regularly. Without shared tooling:
- Each new server is scaffolded from scratch or by copying/adapting existing code
- Quality varies — tool names, descriptions, and schemas follow different conventions
- There is no systematic way to analyze or improve existing tools
- Knowledge about MCP design (spec, best practices, patterns) is scattered or implicit

A dedicated tool that knows the ecosystem, knows the MCP spec, and can generate scaffolds would compound in value: every new project benefits from it, and it can improve over time.

chunks.heading: ADR 004 — uefi-mcpgen as a Dedicated Meta-Tool › Decision
chunks.text:
Create `uefi-mcpgen`: an MCP server specifically for generating, analyzing, and planning AI infrastructure. It is the meta-layer of the ecosystem — a tool about tools.

**Core design principles:**
1. **Instruction Package pattern** — tools return rich context + instructions; Claude generates the actual code. No in-process code generation.
2. **Knowledge base as Markdown** — behavior is tuned by editing `knowledge/*.md`, not code.
3. **Templates as additive** — new template types drop into `templates/<type>/` with zero code changes.
4. **Ecosystem-aware** — knows UEFIabc naming, ADR numbering, conventions, and repo hierarchy.
5. **Self-applicable** — can analyze its own tools and generate improvements to itself.

chunks.heading: ADR 004 — uefi-mcpgen as a Dedicated Meta-Tool › Rationale
chunks.text:
**Why a dedicated repo, not part of uefi-prompts?**
- `uefi-prompts` deals with text artifacts (prompts). `uefi-mcpgen` deals with code artifacts (servers, skills, schemas). Different output types, different templates, different knowledge base.
- Keeping them separate prevents scope creep and keeps each server focused.

**Why Instruction Package instead of code generation?**
- Claude is better at generating contextually-aware code in a conversation than a template engine is at parameterizing it.
- Instruction Package keeps the tool simple (returns a string) and leverages Claude's actual strengths.
- True code generation (writing files) is reserved for the `scaffold_mcp` + user-directed write workflow.

**Why editable Markdown knowledge base?**
- The MCP spec, best practices, and patterns evolve. Editing a `.md` file is far lower friction than modifying Python code.
- Knowledge articles can be versioned and improved independently of the server code.

chunks.heading: ADR 004 — uefi-mcpgen as a Dedicated Meta-Tool › Rationale
chunks.text:
Editing a `.md` file is far lower friction than modifying Python code.
- Knowledge articles can be versioned and improved independently of the server code.

**Why not use uefi-uefimcp as the template base?**
- `uefi-uefimcp` is specialized for educational content (content loader, teaching tools, exercise tools). `uefi-mcpgen` needs a different architecture suited to its meta role.
- Using the wrong template as a base adds technical debt rather than reducing it.

chunks.heading: ADR 004 — uefi-mcpgen as a Dedicated Meta-Tool › Rejected alternatives
chunks.text:
- **Shell scripts for scaffolding** — not AI-aware; produces boilerplate but not contextually-correct code
- **Part of uefi-prompts** — different output type, would create confusion about scope
- **A web app** — infrastructure overhead; a Claude Code-integrated MCP is more natural for this workflow

chunks.heading: ADR 004 — uefi-mcpgen as a Dedicated Meta-Tool › Consequences
chunks.text:
- When creating any new UEFIabc project, `uefi-mcpgen` is the first tool to reach for
- The knowledge base (`knowledge/*.md`) must be updated when the MCP spec or ecosystem conventions change
- Each new template type requires adding files to `templates/<type>/` — convention is `{{VARIABLE}}` placeholders, `.tmpl` extension
- `uefi-context` ADR numbering: the next ADR will be **005**
- `ecosystem.md` in the knowledge base mirrors `uefi-context/docs/conventions.md` — they must be kept in sync when conventions change

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Conventions › Naming
chunks.text:
This document captures shared conventions that apply across all UEFIabc projects.
Add to it as norms emerge — the goal is that an AI (or new contributor) can read this and immediately understand how things are done.

---

- Repository names: `kebab-case`
- Folders inside repos: `kebab-case`
- This context repo is always referred to as `uefi-context`

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Conventions › Decisions
chunks.text:
- Project context files live in `uefi-context/projects/<project-name>.md`
- Each file should open with a one-paragraph summary an AI can use as a quick brief

- Any non-trivial architectural choice gets an ADR in `uefi-context/decisions/`
- ADR filenames: `NNN-short-title.md` (e.g. `001-use-uefi-context-repo.md`)

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Conventions › MCP repos
chunks.text:
- Conversations worth preserving are saved in `uefi-context/conversations/`
- Filename format: `DD-MM-YYYY-topic.md`
- Include the date, participants (human / AI model), and a summary at the top

- All MCP server repos follow the naming pattern: `uefi-<slug>` (e.g. `uefi-bases-matematicas`)
- Every MCP repo is derived from `uefi-uefimcp` (the base template)
- Three-level hierarchy: `uefi-uefimcp` → `uefi-<course>` → `uefi-<subject>`
- Each subject MCP must have a project file in `uefi-context/projects/uefi-<subject>.md`
- Feature flags in `config/subject.json` gate subject-specific capabilities
- Default language for all UFABC subject MCPs: **Portuguese (pt-BR)**

chunks.heading: UEFIabc Conventions › Content files in MCP repos
chunks.text:
- All educational content lives in `content/` and is organized by section: `syllabus/`, `bibliography/`, `exams/`, `exercises/`, `notes/`, `media/`
- Text content preferred: `.md` > `.txt` > `.tex`
- Exercise files should include `<!-- difficulty: easy|medium|hard -->` and `<!-- topic: ... -->` comments for filtering
- Exam files named `MM-YYYY-<type>.md` (e.g. `06-2024-midterm.md`)

---

*This file is a living document. Update it whenever a new cross-project convention is established.*

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen
chunks.text:
`uefi-mcpgen` is the **meta-tool** of the UEFIabc ecosystem. It is an MCP server that helps design, scaffold, analyze, and improve other AI tools — MCP servers, Claude Code skills, tool schemas, and entire architectures.

It is self-referential: it can analyze its own tools and generate improvements to itself or any other repo in the ecosystem.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › MCP tools
chunks.text:
**Complete** (08-04-2026). All tools functional, templates and knowledge base populated.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › MCP tools
chunks.text:
**Complete** (08-04-2026). All tools functional, templates and knowledge base populated.

---

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scaffold_mcp` | Generate a full Python or TypeScript MCP server scaffold |
| `scaffold_skill` | Generate a Claude Code skill (slash command) |
| `scaffold_tool_schema` | Generate a JSON Schema for an MCP tool's `inputSchema` |
| `list_templates` | List all available scaffold templates |
| `analyze_mcp` | Analyze an existing MCP server for quality, completeness, security |
| `analyze_tool_design` | Analyze a single tool's name, description, and schema |
| `analyze_prompt` | Analyze a system/meta prompt for scope, clarity, and audience alignment |
| `suggest_tools` | Propose a complete tool suite for a given domain and use case |
| `suggest_mcp_architecture` | Propose a full internal architecture for a new MCP server |
| `plan_ecosystem_fit` | Determine how a new project fits the UEFIabc ecosystem |
| `get_knowledge` | Retrieve a knowledge base article |
| `generate_context_entry` | Draft `projects/<name>.md` and an ADR for a new project |
| `save_artifact` | Persist a generated artifact to `generated/<type>/` |
| `list_artifacts` | List all stored artifacts, optionally by type |
| `get_artifact` | Retrieve a stored artifact by type and name |
| `search_artifacts` | Full-text search across stored artifacts |
| `save_analysis` | Save a completed analysis to a docs folder (priority: uefi-context/docs → uefi-uefimcp/docs/analysis → generated/analysis) |
| `prepare_edit` | Load an existing file for AI-assisted editing; returns content + editing instructions + relevant knowledge |
| `write_file` | Write edited content back to the file's original path (existing files only) |

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › Generated artifact storage
chunks.text:
All generated content is persisted to `generated/`:

| Folder | Content | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| `generated/skills/` | Claude Code skill files | `.md` |
| `generated/schemas/` | Tool `inputSchema` JSON | `.json` |
| `generated/scaffolds/` | Full MCP scaffold descriptions | `.md` |
| `generated/plans/` | Ecosystem plans and architecture docs | `.md` |
| `generated/analysis/` | Analysis reports (fallback destination) | `.md` |

`save_analysis` prioritizes writing to `uefi-context/docs/` first, then `uefi-uefimcp/docs/analysis/`, falling back to `generated/analysis/`.

All files carry YAML frontmatter (title, type, source_tool, date, tags, notes).
Versioning: if a name conflicts, the new file gets a `-v2`, `-v3` suffix.
Generated artifacts are also exposed as `generated://` MCP resources.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › Knowledge base
chunks.text:
Five articles ground all tool outputs:

| Article | Content |
|---|---|
| `mcp-spec.md` | MCP protocol primitives: tools, resources, prompts; Python and TypeScript SDK basics |
| `best-practices.md` | Tool naming, descriptions, schemas, server organization, anti-patterns |
| `tool-patterns.md` | 7 reusable patterns with code examples; anti-pattern table |
| `skill-spec.md` | Claude Code skill/hook format, design principles, common mistakes |
| `ecosystem.md` | UEFIabc repo naming, hierarchy, conventions, ADR numbering, language defaults |

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › Templates
chunks.text:
| Type | Files |
|---|---|
| `mcp-python` | `pyproject.toml.tmpl`, `server.py.tmpl`, `tool_module.py.tmpl` |
| `mcp-typescript` | `package.json.tmpl`, `tsconfig.json.tmpl`, `src/index.ts.tmpl` |
| `skill` | `skill.md.tmpl` |

All templates use `{{VARIABLE}}` placeholders.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › Key design decisions
chunks.text:
- **Instruction Package pattern** — tools return context + instructions; Claude produces the actual code in the conversation (no in-process code generation)
- **Knowledge base is editable Markdown** — tuning behavior means editing `.md` files in `knowledge/`, not touching code
- **Templates are additive** — new template types drop into `templates/<type>/` with no code changes
- **Self-analysis** — `analyze_mcp` can be pointed at `uefi-mcpgen` itself

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-mcpgen › Related ADR
chunks.text: See `decisions/004-mcpgen-meta-tool.md`.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-prompts
chunks.text:
`uefi-prompts` is a **dual-purpose repository**: a categorized prompt library and an MCP server that generates, rates, and improves prompts.

It is **not** tied to the UFABC MCP subject ecosystem — it is a general-purpose tool for any kind of prompt, though it may store prompts used internally by the UFABC MCPs as well.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-prompts › Status
chunks.text:
| Role | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Library** | Stores prompts in `/library/<category>/`, organized by domain and use case |
| **MCP server** | Exposes tools to generate, rate, improve, search, and save prompts |

---

**Template complete** (08-04-2026). Library is empty — prompts should be added manually or generated via the MCP.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-prompts › MCP tools
chunks.text:
`academic`, `coding`, `creative`, `meta`, `personal`, `professional`, `productivity`, `system`, `teaching`

---

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `list_categories` | Show all categories with prompt counts |
| `list_prompts` | List prompts, optionally filtered by category |
| `get_prompt` | Retrieve a specific prompt by path or slug |
| `search_prompts` | Full-text search across the library |
| `generate_prompt` | Generate a new prompt given goal, category, audience, style |
| `save_prompt` | Save a generated/improved prompt into the library as a `--ai` file |
| `rate_prompt` | Score a prompt on clarity, specificity, robustness, reusability |
| `save_rating` | Persist a rating score into a prompt's frontmatter |
| `improve_prompt` | Rewrite a prompt focusing on specified improvement axes |

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-prompts › Key conventions
chunks.text:
- **AI-generated filenames**: `<slug>--ai.md`, versions as `--ai-v2.md`, `--ai-v3.md`
- **Manually written filenames**: `<slug>.md` (no `--ai` marker)
- **Frontmatter fields**: `title`, `category`, `tags`, `generated_by`, `model`, `rating`, `improved_from`
- **Improvement axes**: `clarity`, `specificity`, `robustness`, `reusability`, `conciseness`, `structure`
- **Rating dimensions**: `clarity`, `specificity`, `robustness`, `reusability` (scored 1–5)

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-prompts › Meta-prompts (the AI's own instructions)
chunks.text:
The MCP uses three internal meta-prompts to do its work:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `meta-prompts/generator.md` | Instructions for writing new prompts |
| `meta-prompts/rater.md` | Instructions for rating prompts on 4 dimensions |
| `meta-prompts/improver.md` | Instructions for rewriting/improving prompts |

These are plain Markdown files — edit them to tune the quality of generated output.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-prompts › Related ADR
chunks.text:
Python 3.11+, `mcp` SDK (stdio), `python-frontmatter` for YAML frontmatter parsing.

---

See `decisions/003-uefi-prompts-dual-purpose.md`.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-tutorial › Conventions
chunks.text:

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-bct
chunks.text:
`uefi-uefimcp-bct` é o **MCP de nível de curso** para o Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia (BCT) da UFABC. É um fork especializado de `uefi-uefimcp`, adaptado para cobrir o BCT como um todo — estrutura curricular, documentos institucionais e navegação acadêmica — em vez de uma única disciplina.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-bct › Propósito
chunks.text: Dar ao Claude conhecimento profundo do curso BCT da UFABC: currículo, requisitos de progressão, documentos oficiais (PPCs), planejamento de oferta e caminhos para o segundo ciclo. Permite ajudar estudantes a navegar o curso e planejar sua jornada acadêmica.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-bct › Status
chunks.text:
```
uefi-uefimcp ← template genérico
 └── uefi-uefimcp-bct ← este repo (nível de curso: BCT)
 └── uefi-<disciplina> ← nível de disciplina (ex: uefi-bases-matematicas)
```

**Configuração inicial completa** (11-04-2026). Conteúdo disponível:
- `content/bibliography/`: PPC 2015, PPC 2023, planejamento oferta 2026, disciplinas limitadas 2025, orientações curricularização extensão
- `content/syllabus/curriculo_bct.md`: síntese estrutural do currículo BCT

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-biotec
chunks.text:
`uefi-uefimcp-biotec` é o **MCP de nível de curso** para o Bacharelado em Biotecnologia (BIOTEC) da UFABC. É um fork especializado de `uefi-uefimcp`, adaptado para cobrir o BIOTEC como um todo — estrutura curricular, documentos institucionais e navegação acadêmica — em vez de uma única disciplina.

---

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-biotec › Propósito
chunks.text: Dar ao Claude conhecimento profundo do curso BIOTEC da UFABC: currículo, requisitos de progressão, documentos oficiais (PPC), planejamento de oferta e áreas de aprofundamento dentro da biotecnologia. Permite ajudar estudantes a navegar o curso e planejar sua jornada acadêmica.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-biotec › Status
chunks.text:
```
uefi-uefimcp ← template genérico
 └── uefi-uefimcp-biotec ← este repo (nível de curso: BIOTEC)
 └── uefi-<disciplina> ← nível de disciplina (ex: uefi-bioquimica)
```

**Configuração inicial completa** (02-06-2026). Conteúdo a adicionar:
- `content/bibliography/`: PPC do curso, planejamento de oferta, listas de disciplinas limitadas
- `content/syllabus/`: síntese estrutural do currículo BIOTEC

chunks.text:

**Específicas do BIOTEC:**
- `get_curriculum_structure` — estrutura curricular completa (obrigatórias, opção limitada, livre escolha, extensão)
- `list_subjects_by_area` — disciplinas agrupadas por área (biologia, bioquímica, microbiologia, genética, bioinformática, química)
- `get_disciplinas_limitadas` — disciplinas com vagas restritas
- `get_progression_requirements` — requisitos de progressão e formatura
- `plan_academic_journey` — planejamento quadrimestral personalizado (parâmetro `research_area` em vez de `target_second_cycle`, pois BIOTEC é segundo ciclo)

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-biotec › Decisões arquiteturais
chunks.text:
- **Suporte a PDF:** opcional via `[pdf]` extra (`pypdf>=4.0`). O `ContentLoader` inclui PDFs automaticamente se `pypdf` estiver instalado. Sem ele, PDFs são silenciosamente ignorados.
- **Feature flag `curriculum_navigation`:** ativa as 5 ferramentas BIOTEC-específicas em `config/subject.json`. As ferramentas do template continuam sempre ativas.
- **`plan_academic_journey` sem `target_second_cycle`:** ao contrário do BCT (primeiro ciclo), estudantes do BIOTEC já escolheram seu curso. O parâmetro equivalente é `research_area` (ex: bioinformática, bioprocessos, farmacotoxicologia).
- **`symbolic_math` habilitado:** disciplinas de bioquímica, biofísica e bioestatística envolvem cálculo e álgebra; mantido consistente com o BCT.
- **Idioma padrão:** Português (pt-BR), conforme convenção do ecossistema.

chunks.text:

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp-engenharias › Decisões arquiteturais
chunks.text:

- **Fork do template direto:** `uefi-uefimcp-engenharias` deriva diretamente de `uefi-uefimcp` (não do BCT), pois as Engenharias são independentes do BCT hierarquicamente.
- **`curriculum.py` criado do zero:** adaptado do BIOTEC com áreas de engenharia e parâmetro `curso`.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp › Purpose
chunks.text:
`uefi-uefimcp` is the **base MCP server template** for the entire UEFIabc educational ecosystem. It is the foundation that every subject-specific MCP repo is built on top of.

---

Provide a reusable, well-structured MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that, when specialized, makes an AI deeply knowledgeable about a specific UFABC university subject. The server exposes the subject's educational content (syllabus, bibliography, past exams, exercises, lecture notes) as tools and resources that Claude can call during a conversation.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp › Status
chunks.text:
```
uefi-uefimcp ← this repo (generic template)
 └── uefi-<course> ← course-level repo (e.g. uefi-science-and-technology)
 └── uefi-<subject> ← subject-level repo (e.g. uefi-precalculus)
```

**Template complete** (08-04-2026). No subject-specific repos have been created yet.

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp › Key architectural decisions
chunks.text:
- **Language:** Python 3.11+ with the `mcp` SDK (stdio transport)
- **Content:** Markdown-first; indexed and searched at runtime by `ContentLoader`
- **Tools exposed:** `get_syllabus`, `get_bibliography`, `get_past_exams`, `search_content`, `get_notes`, `explain_concept`, `get_topic_outline`, `generate_study_plan`, `get_exercises`, `solve_exercise`, `generate_exercise`
- **Prompts:** Three prompt fragments — `system.md` (identity), `teaching.md` (pedagogy), `solver.md` (step-by-step solving)
- **Feature flags:** Subject-specific capabilities (symbolic math, image interpretation, circuit editing) toggled via `config/subject.json`
- **Default language:** Portuguese (pt-BR), matching UFABC's language

chunks.heading: Project: uefi-uefimcp › How to spawn a new subject MCP
chunks.text:
1. Copy/fork `uefi-uefimcp`
2. Rename to `uefi-<subject-slug>`
3. Edit `config/subject.json` — subject name, features, metadata
4. Edit `prompts/system.md` — replace placeholders, tighten scope
5. Populate `content/` with real course materials
6. Add custom tools to `src/tools/` if the subject needs them (e.g. circuit interpretation)
7. Create a project file here in `uefi-context/projects/uefi-<subject>.md`

chunks.heading: uefi-tutorial › Path conventions used in this repo
chunks.text:
All tutorials use placeholder variables in angle brackets. Substitute your actual values everywhere you see them.

| Variable | Meaning | Example |

| `<UFABC_ROOT>` | Root folder containing all UEFIabc repos | `E:\Bibliotecas\Documentos\PROGRAMMING\UEFIabc` |
| `<USERNAME>` | Your Windows username | `Arthur` |
| `<SUBJECT_SLUG>` | kebab-case subject name | `precalculus` |
| `<COURSE_SLUG>` | kebab-case course name | `science-and-technology` |

In bash commands (Claude Code terminal), use forward slashes even on Windows:
```

```

chunks.heading: uefi-tutorial › Glossary
chunks.text:
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — standard for connecting Claude to external tools and data |
| **MCP server** | A local program that exposes tools, resources, and prompts to Claude |
| **Tool** | A callable function Claude can invoke (e.g. `get_syllabus`, `scaffold_mcp`) |
| **Resource** | A URI-addressable file/document Claude can read directly |
| **Prompt** | A reusable message template Claude can invoke by name |
| **Skill** | A Claude Code slash command (e.g. `/commit`) defined in a `.md` file |
| **stdio transport** | Communication via subprocess stdin/stdout — the default for local MCPs |
| **uefi-context** | The ecosystem's context/memory repo — ADRs, project files, conventions |
| **uefi-uefimcp** | Template for all UFABC subject MCPs |
| **uefi-prompts** | Prompt library + MCP to generate/rate/improve prompts |
| **uefi-mcpgen** | Meta-tool MCP — scaffolds, analyzes, and plans other AI tools |

chunks.text:
cp -r uefi-uefimcp uefi-<SUBJECT_SLUG>

cd uefi-<SUBJECT_SLUG>

rm -rf .git
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit from uefi-uefimcp template"
```

> **Windows note:** Use Git Bash or WSL for these commands. Alternatively, copy the folder manually in Explorer and then run `git init` in the new folder.

---

chunks.heading: Remove the template's git history and start fresh › Step 2 — Configure the subject
chunks.text:
Edit `config/subject.json` to identify the subject:

```json
{
 "server_name": "uefi-mcp-<SUBJECT_SLUG>",
 "subject_name": "<SUBJECT_NAME>",
 "course_name": "Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia",
 "institution": "UFABC",
 "language": "pt-BR",

"features": {
 "image_interpretation": false,
 "symbolic_math": false,
 "circuit_editing": false,
 "code_execution": false
 },

"metadata": {
 "credits": <CREDITS>,
 "semester": "<SEMESTER>",
 "professor": "<PROFESSOR>",
 "year": <YEAR>
 }
}
```

**Feature flags** — enable only what the subject needs:

| Feature | Enable for |
|---|---|
| `image_interpretation` | Subjects with diagrams (circuits, graphs, biological structures) |
| `symbolic_math` | Calculus, algebra, discrete math — installs `sympy`, `numpy` |
| `circuit_editing` | Digital circuits, electronics |
| `code_execution` | Programming subjects |

To enable `symbolic_math`, also update the install command in Step 3:
```bash
uv pip install -e ".[math]"
```

---

chunks.heading: If imageinterpretation is enabled:
chunks.text:
```bash
# From inside uefi-<SUBJECT_SLUG>/
uv pip install -e .

uv pip install -e ".[math]"

uv pip install -e ".[vision]"
```

Verify the install:
```bash
python -m src.server --help
# Should exit without error (stdio server has no --help, but import errors would surface here)
```

---

chunks.heading: If imageinterpretation is enabled: › Step 4 — Update the system prompt
chunks.text:
Edit `prompts/system.md`. Replace all `[Subject Name]` placeholders:

```markdown
# System Prompt — <SUBJECT_NAME>

You are a specialized academic assistant for **<SUBJECT_NAME>**,
a course offered at **UFABC (Universidade Federal do ABC)**, Brazil.
...
```

Also update the `## Scope` section to describe what topics are in and out of bounds for this subject.

---

chunks.heading: If imageinterpretation is enabled: › Step 5 — Add content
chunks.text:
Place course materials in the appropriate `content/` subfolder:

| Folder | What to put here | Naming convention |
|---|---|---|
| `content/syllabus/` | Official syllabus `.md` files | `syllabus.md` |
| `content/bibliography/` | Book/article references | `bibliography.md` |
| `content/exams/` | Past exams (scanned → typed as `.md`) | `MM-YYYY-midterm.md` |
| `content/exercises/` | Practice problems by topic | `<topic>-<difficulty>.md` |
| `content/notes/` | Lecture notes, concept sheets | `<topic>.md` |
| `content/media/` | Images, diagrams (if enabled) | `<topic>-diagram.png` |

**Minimum viable content** to start using the MCP:
- [ ] At least one file in `content/syllabus/`
- [ ] At least one file in `content/bibliography/`

The more content you add, the more relevant and grounded Claude's answers will be.

**Content format** (example exercise file):

```markdown
<!-- topic: limits -->
<!-- difficulty: medium -->

chunks.heading: Limits — Medium Exercises › Step 6 — Test the server locally
chunks.text:
Calculate: lim(x→2) (x² - 4) / (x - 2)

Factor the numerator: (x+2)(x-2) / (x-2) = x+2

As x→2: x+2 = 4

**Answer: 4**
```

---

Run the server in your terminal to check for import errors:

```bash
cd "<UFABC_ROOT>\uefi-<SUBJECT_SLUG>"
python -m src.server
```

The server will hang waiting for MCP messages — that is correct. Press `Ctrl+C` to stop it. If you see a Python traceback, fix the error before proceeding.

 --cwd "<UFABC_ROOT>/uefi-<SUBJECT_SLUG>"

Verify it's registered:

```

---

Open Claude Desktop (or a Claude Code session) and ask:

```
What tools does the uefi-<SUBJECT_SLUG> MCP expose?
```

Expected response: a list including `get_syllabus`, `get_bibliography`, `get_past_exams`, `search_content`, `get_notes`, `explain_concept`, `get_topic_outline`, `generate_study_plan`, `get_exercises`, `solve_exercise`, `generate_exercise`.

Then test a real query:

```

```

chunks.heading: Limits — Medium Exercises › Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Server not appearing in Claude | Config file syntax error | Validate JSON at [jsonlint.com](https://jsonlint.com) |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: mcp` | Dependencies not installed | Run `uv pip install -e .` again |
| `No syllabus content loaded` | `content/syllabus/` is empty | Add at least one `.md` file |
| Tool returns empty results | Content files not `.md`/`.txt` | Check file extensions |
| Server crashes on start | `config/subject.json` syntax error | Validate the JSON |

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Variables
chunks.text:
By the end of this tutorial you will have the `uefi-prompts` MCP running and connected to Claude. You'll be able to generate new prompts, rate existing ones, improve them, and browse the growing library — all through natural conversation.

---

| Variable | Your value | Example |

| `<UFABC_ROOT>` | Path to your UEFIabc repos folder | `E:\Bibliotecas\Documentos\PROGRAMMING\UEFIabc` |
| `<USERNAME>` | Your Windows username | `Arthur` |

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Step 1 — Install dependencies
chunks.text:
- Python 3.11+ installed (`python --version`)
- `uv` installed (`pip install uv`)
- `uefi-prompts` repo already cloned inside `<UFABC_ROOT>`
- Claude Desktop or Claude Code

---

```bash
cd "<UFABC_ROOT>\uefi-prompts"
pip install -e .
```

This installs:
- `mcp` — the MCP SDK
- `pydantic` — data validation
- `anyio` — async runtime
- `python-frontmatter` — YAML frontmatter parser (reads prompt metadata)

Verify:
```bash
python -c "import mcp; import frontmatter; print('OK')"
```

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Step 2 — Understand the directory layout
chunks.text:
```
uefi-prompts/
├── library/ ← your prompt collection lives here
│ ├── academic/
│ ├── coding/
│ ├── creative/
│ ├── meta/
│ ├── personal/
│ ├── professional/
│ ├── productivity/
│ ├── system/
│ └── teaching/
├── meta-prompts/ ← instructions the MCP uses internally
│ ├── generator.md
│ ├── rater.md
│ └── improver.md
└── src/server.py ← entry point
```

**Key concept:** The `library/` folder is the persistent storage. Every prompt — whether you wrote it manually or the MCP generated it — ends up as a `.md` file here. AI-generated files are marked with `--ai` in their filename (e.g., `explain-recursion--ai.md`).

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Step 3 — Add your first manual prompt (optional)
chunks.text:
Before connecting to Claude, you can seed the library with a prompt you already use:

1. Choose a category (e.g., `teaching`)
2. Create a file: `library/teaching/my-first-prompt.md`

```markdown
---
title: "Explain a concept step by step"
category: teaching
tags: ["explanation", "step-by-step"]
generated_by: human
model: null
rating: null
---

Explain {{concept}} step by step. Start with the intuition (why it matters),
then the mechanism (how it works), then give one concrete example.
Use simple language. End with a one-sentence summary.
```

This file will immediately be searchable once the server starts.

---

chunks.text:

python -m src.server

No traceback = the server is ready to connect.

C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Roaming\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json

Add or merge this entry:

```json
{

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Step 7 — First use: generate a prompt › Generate
chunks.text:
In Claude, ask:

```
List all prompt categories in uefi-prompts.
```

Expected: a list of the 9 categories with their prompt counts.

---

Try each of the three core workflows:

```
Generate a prompt for the coding category. Goal: help a developer write clear
commit messages. Style: instruction. Audience: software developers.
Save it to the library when done.
```

Claude will call `generate_prompt`, produce the prompt text, then call `save_prompt`. The result lands in `library/coding/<slug>--ai.md`.

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Step 7 — First use: generate a prompt › Improve
chunks.text:
```
Rate the prompt at library/coding/<slug>--ai.md
```

Claude calls `rate_prompt` and returns scores on clarity, specificity, robustness, and reusability with improvement suggestions.

```
Improve the prompt at library/coding/<slug>--ai.md, focusing on clarity and robustness. Save the improved version.
```

Claude calls `improve_prompt` and `save_prompt`. The result is `library/coding/<slug>--ai-v2.md`.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Tuning the generator quality
chunks.text:
The meta-prompts in `meta-prompts/` control how the MCP generates and rates prompts. They are plain Markdown — edit them to change behavior:

| File | Controls |
|---|---|
| `meta-prompts/generator.md` | How new prompts are written |
| `meta-prompts/rater.md` | The scoring rubric and output format |
| `meta-prompts/improver.md` | Rewrite strategy per improvement axis |

No code changes needed — just edit the `.md` files and restart the server.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 02 — Setup uefi-prompts › Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `ModuleNotFoundError: frontmatter` | Run `uv pip install python-frontmatter` |
| Library shows 0 prompts | Check that files in `library/` have `.md` extension and valid frontmatter |
| `save_prompt` fails | Ensure the `category` matches one of the 9 defined categories |
| Generated prompt is low quality | Edit `meta-prompts/generator.md` and restart the server |

---

uefi-mcpgen/

│ ├── mcp-spec.md MCP protocol reference

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › What you'll accomplish
chunks.text:
You'll run the same task twice — once with a raw prompt typed directly into Claude, and once using a structured approach (an MCP tool or a skill). You'll observe the difference in output quality, consistency, and depth, and you'll learn when each method is the right choice.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › The task
chunks.text:
- `uefi-mcpgen` MCP connected to Claude (Tutorial 03 completed)
- Claude Desktop or Claude Code
- Basic familiarity with what MCP tools are

---

We'll use: **"Review the design of an MCP tool and suggest improvements."**

This is a real task you'll do regularly as you build UEFIabc tools. It's a good benchmark because:
- A generic prompt produces useful but inconsistent output
- A structured approach (grounded in `best-practices.md` and `tool-patterns.md`) produces systematic, actionable output with a defined format

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › The tool we'll analyze
Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Method A — Generic prompt
Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Method A — Generic prompt › What to observe in the response
chunks.text:
Note the following about Claude's answer:

- **Does it have a defined structure?** Or does it vary each time you ask?
- **Does it evaluate specific dimensions** (name clarity, description quality, schema completeness)? Or does it give general impressions?
- **Does it reference a standard** (best practices, common patterns)? Or does it reason from first principles?
- **Does it give a score or ranking?** Or just prose?
- **Is the advice actionable?** "Make the description more specific" vs. "Rename to `get_notes` and describe it as: 'Retrieve lecture notes, optionally filtered by topic.'"

Save the response somewhere — you'll compare it in a moment.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Method B — Structured approach via uefi-mcpgen tool
chunks.text:
Now, with `uefi-mcpgen` connected, ask Claude:

```
Use uefi-mcpgen's analyze_tool_design tool to review this tool:

tool_name: "get"
 tool_description: "Get things"
 input_schema: '{"type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "string"}}, "required": []}'
 context: "MCP server for retrieving UFABC lecture notes"
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Method B — Structured approach via uefi-mcpgen tool › What to observe
chunks.text:
Read the structured response. It will evaluate:

1. **Name clarity** — Is "get" a clear verb+noun?
2. **Description quality** — Does "Get things" tell Claude when to call this tool?
3. **Schema completeness** — Is `x` described? Is `required` correct?
4. **Return value** — Is it clear what the tool returns?
5. **Anti-patterns** — Does it violate any of the patterns in `tool-patterns.md`?

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Side-by-side comparison
chunks.text:
| Dimension | Method A (generic) | Method B (structured) |
|---|---|---|
| **Structure** | Varies per run | Always the same 6-point evaluation |
| **Standards reference** | Implicit — Claude's general knowledge | Explicit — grounded in `best-practices.md` and `tool-patterns.md` |
| **Specificity** | "Make the name clearer" | "Rename to `get_notes` (verb+noun, snake_case)" |
| **Actionability** | Medium — suggestions are general | High — each point ends with a concrete fix |
| **Consistency** | Will differ if you ask again | Reproducible — same context, same structure |
| **Context awareness** | None — doesn't know this is a UFABC tool | Aware — `context` param informs the review |

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › When to use each method › Use a structured skill/tool when:
chunks.text:
- You need a quick, exploratory answer
- The task is one-off and the quality bar is "good enough"
- You're iterating fast and don't need reproducible output
- You're outside the domain of any available MCP or skill

- You'll repeat this task more than once (e.g., reviewing tools as you build them)
- You need the output to follow a specific format (for documentation, tracking, etc.)
- You want the output grounded in domain knowledge (best practices, patterns, conventions)
- You want to compare results across different inputs consistently

**Rule of thumb:** If you'd write the same prompt more than twice, it should be a skill or an MCP tool.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Part 2 — Generate a skill for this workflow
chunks.text:
Now let's make Method B even more convenient by creating a permanent skill:

```
Use uefi-mcpgen to scaffold a skill called review-tool.
Description: Analyze an MCP tool definition for design quality.
Behavior: The user pastes a tool definition (name, description, inputSchema).
Use uefi-mcpgen's analyze_tool_design to evaluate it on 6 dimensions and
return specific, actionable fixes for each.
Trigger examples:
 - "When the user asks to review a tool"
 - "When the user types /review-tool"
Save the skill.
```

Claude calls `scaffold_skill` and `save_artifact`. The skill file lands in `generated/skills/review-tool.md`.

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Part 2 — Generate a skill for this workflow › Install the skill
chunks.text:
Copy the generated skill file to your Claude Code skills folder:

**Windows path:**
```
C:\Users\<USERNAME>\.claude\skills\review-tool.md
```

**Bash command:**
```bash
cp "<UFABC_ROOT>/uefi-mcpgen/generated/skills/review-tool.md" \
 "C:/Users/<USERNAME>/.claude/skills/review-tool.md"
```

Now in any Claude Code session you can type:
```
/review-tool
```
and paste your tool definition. Claude will run the full structured analysis without you needing to remember to connect `uefi-mcpgen` or formulate the request.

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Method C — Using a pre-generated skill vs. a live tool call
chunks.text:
There is a subtle third dimension worth understanding:

| | Live MCP tool call | Installed skill file |
|---|---|---|
| **Requires MCP connected** | Yes | No — skill is self-contained |
| **Knowledge base grounding** | Yes — calls `analyze_tool_design` which loads `best-practices.md` live | Partial — skill contains the instructions but not the live knowledge base |
| **Updatable** | Edit `knowledge/best-practices.md`, restart server | Edit the `.md` file directly |
| **Best for** | Maximum quality, live knowledge | Convenience, offline use, no MCP needed |

**Practical guidance:** Use live MCP tools when working actively on UEFIabc repos (Claude will have the full knowledge base). Use installed skills for quick tasks outside the ecosystem or when you don't want to start the MCP server.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 04 — Generic Prompt vs. Structured Skill › Summary
chunks.text:
- **Generic prompt** → flexible, fast, inconsistent
- **MCP tool call** → structured, grounded, consistent, requires server
- **Installed skill** → convenient, self-contained, works offline

The most powerful workflow is to use `uefi-mcpgen` to generate a skill from an MCP tool's behavior, install the skill, and use it as a persistent shortcut.

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › What you'll accomplish
chunks.text:
You'll learn the two types of resources `uefi-mcpgen` exposes — **non-generated** (knowledge base and templates, baked into the repo) and **generated** (artifacts you create at runtime) — and how to use each type in both UEFIabc projects and personal projects outside the ecosystem.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 1 — Understanding the three resource schemes
chunks.text:
- `uefi-mcpgen` connected to Claude (Tutorial 03 completed)
- At least one other project you're working on (can be anything)

---

When `uefi-mcpgen` is connected, Claude can read three URI schemes as MCP resources:

| Scheme | Path | What's there |
|---|---|---|
| `knowledge://` | `knowledge/<name>` | Grounding articles — MCP spec, best practices, patterns, skill spec, ecosystem |
| `template://` | `templates/<type>/<file>.tmpl` | Scaffold templates with `{{VARIABLE}}` placeholders |
| `generated://` | `generated/<type>/<file>` | Artifacts you've saved — skills, schemas, scaffolds, plans |

You can access any of these directly in conversation:

```
Read the resource knowledge://best-practices
```

```
Read the resource template://mcp-python/server.py.tmpl
```

```
Read the resource generated://plans/uefi-thermodynamics.md
```

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 2 — Non-generated resources: knowledge base › What it contains
chunks.text:
Five articles that define how Claude reasons when you use any `uefi-mcpgen` tool:

| Article | Use it when you want to... |
|---|---|
| `mcp-spec` | Understand what tools, resources, and prompts can do |
| `best-practices` | Check naming conventions, schema rules, anti-patterns |
| `tool-patterns` | Find a pattern that fits your tool's behavior |
| `skill-spec` | Understand Claude Code skill/hook format |
| `ecosystem` | Orient a new project within UEFIabc |

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 2 — Non-generated resources: knowledge base › Using knowledge articles in a UFABC project
chunks.text:
**Scenario:** You're designing a new tool for `uefi-precalculus` and aren't sure whether to expose data as a resource or a tool.

```
Read knowledge://mcp-spec from uefi-mcpgen and tell me when to use
resources vs. tools in an MCP server. I'm designing uefi-precalculus
and wondering whether lecture notes should be resources or tool outputs.
```

Claude reads the spec article and applies it to your specific question.

**Scenario:** You've just written a new tool and want to verify it follows conventions.

```
Check this tool definition against knowledge://best-practices and knowledge://tool-patterns:

name: "get_notes"
 description: "Retrieve lecture notes"
 inputSchema: { "type": "object", "properties": {} }
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 2 — Non-generated resources: knowledge base › Using knowledge articles in a personal project
chunks.text:
Knowledge articles are domain-neutral — they teach MCP design, not UFABC content. Use them for any project:

```
I'm building a personal MCP server to manage my reading list.
Read knowledge://tool-patterns and suggest which patterns apply to a tool
that retrieves books by genre and another that marks a book as read.
```

```
I'm designing a skill for Claude Code that helps me write daily standup notes.
Read knowledge://skill-spec and tell me what frontmatter fields I need.
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 2 — Non-generated resources: knowledge base › Editing knowledge articles to tune behavior
chunks.text:
The knowledge base is plain Markdown — editing it changes how Claude reasons across **all** `uefi-mcpgen` tools immediately after a server restart.

**Example:** You've standardized on always including a `language` parameter in your tools' return values. Add this to `knowledge/best-practices.md`:

```markdown
### Language tagging
All tools that return text content must include a `language` parameter
(enum: "pt-BR", "en-US") so Claude can localize its response.
```

After restarting the server, `scaffold_mcp`, `analyze_mcp`, and `suggest_tools` will all reflect this rule automatically.

---

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 3 — Non-generated resources: templates › What templates are
chunks.text:
Template files in `templates/` are the raw scaffolds for generated code. They use `{{VARIABLE}}` placeholders.

```
templates/
├── mcp-python/
│ ├── pyproject.toml.tmpl Python package config
│ ├── server.py.tmpl MCP server entry point
│ └── tool_module.py.tmpl Tool registration module
├── mcp-typescript/
│ ├── package.json.tmpl
│ ├── tsconfig.json.tmpl
│ └── src/index.ts.tmpl
└── skill/
 └── skill.md.tmpl
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 3 — Non-generated resources: templates › Using templates in a personal project
chunks.text:
```
Show me the template://mcp-python/server.py.tmpl resource.
```

This is useful when you want to understand the pattern before generating, or when you want to manually adapt it.

**Scenario:** You want to build a personal MCP server for managing your recipes, but you want to understand the structure before running `scaffold_mcp`.

```
Read template://mcp-python/server.py.tmpl and template://mcp-python/tool_module.py.tmpl.
Then explain to me how the tool registration pattern works, so I can write
a tool called get_recipes manually.
```

**Scenario:** You want to add a new template type for a pattern you use often.

1. Create a new folder: `templates/my-pattern/`
2. Add `.tmpl` files using `{{VARIABLE}}` placeholders
3. Restart the server — `list_templates` will pick it up automatically
4. Use it by telling Claude: *"Use the my-pattern template to scaffold..."*

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 4 — Generated resources: the artifact store › What gets saved here
chunks.text:
Everything you generate through `uefi-mcpgen` and explicitly save with `save_artifact`:

```
generated/
├── skills/ Claude Code skill .md files
├── schemas/ Tool inputSchema .json files
├── scaffolds/ Full MCP scaffold descriptions .md
└── plans/ Ecosystem plans and architecture suggestions .md
```

Files carry YAML frontmatter:
```yaml
---
title: "uefi-thermodynamics scaffold"
type: scaffolds
source_tool: scaffold_mcp
tags: ["ufabc", "physics", "python"]
date: 2026-04-08
notes: "Generated during initial planning session"
---
```

Versioning is automatic: if you save a second artifact with the same slug, it becomes `-v2`, `-v3`, etc.

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 4 — Generated resources: the artifact store › Using generated resources in a personal project
chunks.text:
Generated artifacts are not UFABC-specific. They're reusable across any project.

**Scenario:** You scaffolded a personal MCP for your reading list last month. You want to build a similar one for recipes.

```
Get the generated scaffold for my-reading-list-mcp.
Adapt it to a new server called my-recipes-mcp with these tools:
 - get_recipes (filtered by cuisine or ingredient)
 - add_recipe (save a new recipe)
 - rate_recipe (score 1-5)
```

Claude loads the existing scaffold as a reference and adapts it, inheriting all the patterns you established in the original.

**Scenario:** You saved a schema for a tool pattern you reuse often.

```
Get the generated schema named pagination-params.
Apply it as a parameter group to the get_recipes tool — recipes should
support offset/limit pagination.
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 5 — Full workflow: a personal project from scratch › Goal: build a personal MCP for tracking study sessions
chunks.text:
Here's a complete end-to-end workflow for a personal project, using all resource types:

**Step 1 — Check what patterns apply (knowledge)**
```
Read knowledge://tool-patterns. Which patterns apply to a CRUD-like server
that tracks study sessions (create session, list sessions, get stats)?
```

**Step 2 — Suggest the tool suite**
```
Use suggest_tools: domain "study session tracking", use case "personal productivity",
user actions: log a session, list sessions by subject, get weekly stats, set goals.
```

**Step 3 — Scaffold the server**
```
Use scaffold_mcp: name "my-study-tracker", Python, with the tools from the suggestion above.
Save the scaffold.
```

**Step 4 — Generate a skill for the most frequent action**
```
Use scaffold_skill: name "log-study", behavior: prompt me for subject, duration, and notes,
then call the my-study-tracker MCP to log the session. Save it.
```

**Step 5 — Install the skill**
```bash
cp "<UFABC_ROOT>/uefi-mcpgen/generated/skills/log-study.md" \
 "C:/Users/<USERNAME>/.claude/skills/log-study.md"
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Part 5 — Full workflow: a personal project from scratch › Goal: build a personal MCP for tracking study sessions
chunks.text:
Save it.
```

**Step 5 — Install the skill**
```bash
cp "<UFABC_ROOT>/uefi-mcpgen/generated/skills/log-study.md" \
 "C:/Users/<USERNAME>/.claude/skills/log-study.md"
```

**Step 6 — Later, retrieve and build**
```
Retrieve the scaffold for my-study-tracker and generate all source files.
```

chunks.heading: Tutorial 05 — Using uefi-mcpgen Resources in Any Project › Summary
chunks.text:
| Resource type | URI scheme | How to use |
|---|---|---|
| Knowledge articles | `knowledge://` | Read directly, or let `uefi-mcpgen` tools use them automatically |
| Templates | `template://` | Read to understand patterns; edit to change scaffold output |
| Generated artifacts | `generated://` | Save with `save_artifact`; retrieve with `get_artifact`; browse with `list_artifacts` |

**The compound value**: the longer you use `uefi-mcpgen`, the more artifacts you accumulate. Each new project can reference previous ones — you're building a personal library of AI tool patterns, not just one-off scaffolds.

DE ATIVIDADES COMPLEMENTARES.

ATIVIDADES COMPLEMENTARES PELA PROGRAD, sendo que ambas devem ser submetidas pelo SIGAA.

PARA OS ESTUDANTES DE PPCs ANTERIORES A 2023: nós da Coordenação do BC&T não recomendamos a troca de PPC a não ser que você seja bolsista ou voluntário de projetos/programas de extensão que lhe garantirão 240 horas de extensão, lembrando que estas horas devem ter sido realizadas OBRIGATORIAMENTE A PARTIR DE 2023.

Tal recomendação se deve ao fato que infelizmente por falta de informação ou ruído na comunicação, muitos estudantes estão fazendo a migração sem avaliar as dificuldades de realização das horas de extensão (que só serão aceitas se tiverem sido realizadas a partir de 2023), bem como uma forma de não precisar cursar IAM (Interações Atômico Moleculares), lembrando que o tempo de dedicação à IAM é muito inferior ao de 240 horas de extensão, uma vez que é uma disciplina de 36h ofertada todo 1º quadrimestre.

Cursar 36h é muito mais plausível do que 240h de atividades que inevitavelmente terão que ser realizadas fora de turno de aula.

PARA OS ESTUDANTES DO PPCs 2023: recomendamos fortemente que se faça atividades de extensão todo quadrimestre para que se consiga obter as 240h necessárias para a integralização do seu curso.

Lembre-se que você pode atuar como voluntário de projetos/programas de extensão para além da participação em eventos de extensão.

Para buscar um projeto que seja de seu interesse você pode buscar em:

chunks.heading: Obrigatórias Do Bc&t - 2026
chunks.text:
À comunidade acadêmica,

Apresentamos o planejamento de oferta de disciplinas obrigatórias do BC&T, para o ano letivo de 2026, para cada um dos três quadrimestres. É importante salientar que neste planejamento levamos em conta a grade sugerida para alunos que ingressaram em 2025, assim como aqueles que ingressarão em 2026 (PPC BC&T 2023).O planejamento de oferta de disciplinas obrigatórias do curso de 2026 foi construído com a colaboração das direções dos Centros, coordenadores de cursos (de ingresso e dos específicos), da CGCG, da CLD e da PROGRAD. Para tal, a Coordenação do BC&T baseou sua proposta no projeto pedagógico do curso, nas normativas estabelecidas na UFABC (resoluções ConsEP Nº 74, ConsUNI nº 47, ConsEP nº 31, relatório do GT-40) e em estudos de ocupação das vagas dos últimos anos.Como tem sido realizado nos anos anteriores, o oferecimento de Projeto Dirigido ocorrerá nos três quadrimestres letivos, em função de limitações de infraestrutura e disponibilidade de corpo docente.

chunks.heading: Obrigatórias Do Bc&t - 2026
chunks.text:
tem sido realizado nos anos anteriores, o oferecimento de Projeto Dirigido ocorrerá nos três quadrimestres letivos, em função de limitações de infraestrutura e disponibilidade de corpo docente.

Lembramos que a partir de 2023, conforme o PPC, os alunos ingressantes serão selecionados para uma das três disciplinas de Humanidades (matrícula automática em 2026.2).Apresentamos também neste documento a quantidade de turmas planejada para cada disciplina.De posse das informações necessárias para a matrícula, é fundamental que os alunos façam suas escolhas por disciplinas com critério e planejem sua trajetória acadêmica por todo o ano letivo, evitando matricular-se em um número maior de disciplinas do que pretende cursar, garantido que tenha as condições para se dedicar e realizar bem as disciplinas.A Coordenação do BC&T reforça que a matrícula consciente é a melhor forma de garantirmos que os recursos estão sendo bem utilizados e que todos os estudantes tenham oportunidade de avançar adequadamente em suas trajetórias escolhidas.

chunks.heading: Obrigatórias Do Bc&t - 2026
chunks.text:
matrícula consciente é a melhor forma de garantirmos que os recursos estão sendo bem utilizados e que todos os estudantes tenham oportunidade de avançar adequadamente em suas trajetórias escolhidas.

Além disso, devemos ressaltar que a alocação de docentes é realizada pelos Centros, e mesmo com planejamento prévio, algumas alterações na oferta poderão ocorrer, principalmente após a matrícula dos alunos, já que a reorganização da oferta de turmas requer também uma reorganização dos docentes.

Um ano letivo de 2026 bastante proveitoso a todos.

Coordenação do Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia

chunks.heading: Apresentação
chunks.text:
A Universidade Federal do ABC foi criada num contexto histórico de

inserção no Grande ABC paulista, espaço que congrega importantes complexos

industriais, elevado grau de urbanização e reservas naturais destinadas à

preservação ambiental. Ao abrigar indústrias de ponta, intensivas em tecnologia

e, ao mesmo tempo, estar cercada de graves problemas sociais e de organização

do espaço metropolitano, a região é um locus de manifestação da mesma

agenda de desafios colocados para o país. Assim, a Instituição busca ser

reconhecida como uma referência no panorama nacional e internacional, por

meio de sua atenção a essas demandas regionais, produzindo pesquisas e

formando profissionais de alta qualidade para enfrentá-las.

Nesse contexto, é oferecido o Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia

(BC&T), um Bacharelado Interdisciplinar entendido, conforme os Referenciais

Orientadores

diploma, com foco na interdisciplinaridade, no diálogo entre as áreas do

conhecimento e na flexibilidade curricular. Ao priorizar em sua estrutura

chunks.heading: Apresentação
chunks.text:
Ao priorizar em sua estrutura

curricular arranjos interdisciplinares que consideram as correlações entre a

realidade sociocultural e ambiental em que se insere, o Projeto Pedagógico do

BC&T ressalta, por sua vez, a importância de uma formação integral nas

ciências, incluindo a visão histórica da nossa civilização e privilegiando a

capacidade de inserção social no sentido amplo.

Assim, o curso tem como meta a criação de um ambiente acadêmico

favorável ao desenvolvimento social, contribuindo para a busca de soluções para

problemas regionais e nacionais, a partir da cooperação com outras instituições

de ensino e pesquisa, bem como com instâncias do setor industrial e dos poderes

executivo, legislativo e judiciário. O caráter inovador do BC&T revelou-se capaz

de consubstanciar uma face da dimensão social da Universidade, ao reconhecer

que uma das tarefas urgentes para assegurar a equidade é democratizar a

excelência científica.

Para promover tal democratização, a Universidade considera a população

do Grande ABC paulista - mais de 2,5 milhões de habitantes, distribuída em 827

necessários ao progresso da sociedade brasileira, à promoção e estímulo de

A organização acadêmica em Centros, sem Departamentos, é outra

escolha institucional que favorece a formação de grupos de pesquisa

interdisciplinares e a participação dos alunos em atividades desse âmbito a partir

de seu ingresso na Universidade. Instigados a aprofundarem a pesquisa durante

toda a vida acadêmica, podem continuar a desenvolvê-la em torno dos

programas de pós-graduação, classificados em categorias disciplinares ou

multidisciplinares.

A UFABC contribui, por meio de atividades de extensão, com o

desenvolvimento cultural, material e humano da comunidade. Dado o forte

caráter social da UFABC, são planejadas e desenvolvidas ações sociais com o

objetivo de beneficiar a comunidade local, em primeira instância, e depois nos

caráter social da UFABC, são planejadas e desenvolvidas ações sociais com o

objetivo de beneficiar a comunidade local, em primeira instância, e depois nos

níveis regional e nacional, com soluções que impactem diretamente na melhoria

da qualidade de vida da população.

O documento apresentado aqui é uma síntese de um processo de

avaliação do BC&T da UFABC e revisão do projeto pedagógico do curso (PPC).

Esse processo foi organizado propiciando a discussão, sempre aberta e coletiva,

dos componentes curriculares que compõem as disciplinas obrigatórias do BC&T.

Para conseguir compilar em um documento todas as impressões da comunidade

e os resultados das discussões ocorridas, a coordenação do BC&T e o Núcleo

chunks.heading: Perfil Do Curso
chunks.text:
O BC&T é um dos cursos obrigatórios de ingresso dos alunos na UFABC e

está pautado nos conceitos de interdisciplinaridade e flexibilidade de

formação profissional. Sua estrutura é baseada no regime quadrimestral e em

um sistema de créditos que permite diferentes organizações curriculares,

conforme os interesses e aptidões dos alunos. Diferente do sistema

educacional universitário tradicional, os alunos são encorajados a se tornarem

responsáveis pela elaboração de sua trajetória acadêmica, ao invés de

serem igualmente conduzidos .

Há na UFABC o comprometimento de se preservar a ideia de liberdade

para a exploração de novos caminhos em todas as atividades acadêmicas.

chunks.heading: Justificativa De Oferta Do Curso
chunks.text:
A dinâmica contemporânea de construção do conhecimento e da

transmissão da informação tem um reflexo particularmente significativo. A

velocidade com que os novos conhecimentos científicos e tecnológicos são

gerados, difundidos, distribuídos e absorvidos pela sociedade em geral elimina

das instituições educacionais a responsabilidade exclusiva de transmissoras de

informações. Assim, há uma ênfase nas atribuições mais complexas de

A transformação da aprendizagem em um processo autônomo e contínuo

para os egressos dos cursos torna-se uma das grandes responsabilidades de

todos os níveis educacionais e, principalmente, do ensino superior. Tal formação

implica não apenas o domínio de tecnologias de informação e comunicação, mas

também o acesso aos conhecimentos socialmente e historicamente acumulados,

mas também a capacidade de selecioná-los, segundo critérios de relevância,

rigor e ética; de reorganizá-los e de produzi-los autonomamente.

Na sociedade atual, o conhecimento ocupa papel central e as pessoas

precisam lidar com ele tanto como cidadãos, quanto como profissionais. A ciência

passa a ser não só um bem cultural, mas também a base do desenvolvimento

econômico e social. No mundo do trabalho, a produtividade está diretamente

associada à produção de novos conhecimentos científicos e técnicos, à introdução

chunks.heading: Justificativa De Oferta Do Curso
chunks.text:
No mundo do trabalho, a produtividade está diretamente

associada à produção de novos conhecimentos científicos e técnicos, à introdução

de inovações, à aplicação de conhecimentos. Os espaços de trabalho tornam-se

cada vez mais espaços de formação e, assim, é cada vez mais imperioso que as

instituições educacionais se aproximem deles.

Os aspectos sociais, tecnológicos e econômicos que caracterizam o mundo

pós-moderno se constituem em argumento suficiente para propor um novo

paradigma na formação dos jovens universitários nas áreas tecnológicas e

científicas. Sobretudo, para torná-los capazes de enfrentar problemas novos sem

receios, com confiança nas suas potencialidades, demonstrando capacidade de

investigação e inovação.

O BC&T é um curso construído com as bases inovadoras de um

Bacharelado Interdisciplinar. Trata-se, portanto, de uma configuração de

percurso acadêmico que está em harmonia com tendências nacionais e

internacionais, sendo uma das opções de curso de ingresso do aluno na

Universidade, que propicia uma formação sólida e diversificada.

chunks.heading: Objetivo Geral
chunks.text:
O objetivo do BC&T é formar o aluno para atuar como pesquisador, gestor e

consultor nas áreas de desenvolvimento científico e tecnológico. Também poderá

atuar na realização de tarefas e na solução de problemas relacionados à sua área

de atuação e atender a funções de natureza estratégica, requeridas na geração

de novos conhecimentos, e nos processos de produção e serviços, seja na área

tecnológica, ambiental ou de sustentabilidade.

chunks.heading: Objetivos Específicos
chunks.text:
Constituem objetivos específicos:

I. Fornecer uma base ampla e profunda no que diz respeito à Informática,

Computação Científica, às Ciências Naturais, às Ciências de Engenharia e à

Matemática;

II. Atender as demandas das tecnologias modernas e emergentes permitindo

uma inserção mais rápida dos formandos na sociedade moderna;

III. Desenvolver questões e temas de cunho epistemológico, histórico, e social

que estimulem a capacidade crítica do estudante no exercício da atividade

profissional e da cidadania;

IV. Desenvolver nos estudantes as habilidades de descobrir, inventar e criticar,

características das Ciências Naturais, das Engenharias e das Matemáticas; e

V. Personalizar o currículo de modo que o aluno possa desenhar sua formação

profissionalizante de acordo com sua vocação e suas aspirações.

Tais objetivos devem ser alcançados oferecendo ao aluno um curso que

fomente a reflexão e a análise fundamentada sobre a prática da ação docente em

todos os seus aspectos: a investigação científica, uma sólida formação em

chunks.heading: Objetivos Específicos
chunks.text:
alcançados oferecendo ao aluno um curso que

fomente a reflexão e a análise fundamentada sobre a prática da ação docente em

todos os seus aspectos: a investigação científica, uma sólida formação em

ciência e tecnologia e a articulação teoria-prática. As disciplinas propostas na

matriz curricular que caracterizam a essência e o caráter interdisciplinar do

curso, bem como o quadro docente altamente qualificado, constituído

integralmente por professores doutores envolvidos em atividades de pesquisa,

além dos recursos de infraestrutura (laboratórios, informática e biblioteca) e de

apoio ao aluno (bolsas socioeconômicas, de iniciação científica, programa de

tutoria) constituem sólidos suportes para a permanência dos alunos e o

cumprimento dos objetivos previstos.

chunks.heading: Forma De Acesso Ao Curso
chunks.text:
A seleção anual de candidatos é realizada por meio do Sistema de Seleção

Unificada (SISU), gerenciado pelo Ministério da Educação (MEC), que considera a

nota obtida no Exame Nacional de Ensino Médio (Enem). Conforme edital de

ingresso nos Bacharelados Interdisciplinares em 2014 (edital nº172/2013), o

BC&T oferece, em São Bernardo do Campo, 435 (quatrocentos e trinta e cinco)

vagas, sendo 217 vagas no matutino e 218 vagas no noturno. No câmpus Santo

André, são oferecidas, por sua vez, 1125 (um mil, cento e vinte e cinco) vagas,

sendo 562 (quinhentos e sessenta e duas) vagas matutinas e 563 (quinhentos e

sessenta e três) vagas no noturno. Nesse edital, destaca-se que, independente

do câmpus de ingresso - São Bernardo ou Santo André - reserva-se ao discente

o direito de participar de atividades acadêmicas de graduação em todos os

câmpus da UFABC. As vagas ofertadas no último processo seletivo tiveram 3

(três) modalidades de concorrência:

a) vagas reservadas para estudantes oriundos de escolas públicas;

b) vagas reservadas para Pessoas com Deficiência (PcD);

O acesso às disciplinas na UFABC

não é regrado pelos tradicionais pré-requisitos . Por outro lado, esse acesso

não ocorre de forma indiscriminada. No Catálogo de Disciplinas de Graduação e

nos Planos de Ensino que constam deste Projeto Pedagógico, são apontadas

recomendações de conhecimentos fundamentais para pleno entendimento e

aproveitamento da disciplina em questão. Tais conhecimentos são indicados

através de uma lista das disciplinas oferecidas pela UFABC. Caso o aluno não

possua o conjunto de conhecimentos indicado, é altamente recomendável que

as disciplinas a eles associadas sejam cursadas antes da disciplina pretendida. A

inexistência de pré-requisitos possibilita aos alunos o exercício da sua autonomia

nos momentos de matrícula. Essa autonomia, reiteramos, deve ser exercida com

responsabilidade .

chunks.heading: Perfil Do Egresso
chunks.text:
O Bacharel em Ciência e Tecnologia atua, de forma generalista, como

pesquisador, gestor, analista e consultor nas áreas de desenvolvimento científico

e tecnológico, na realização de tarefas e na solução de problemas relacionados à

sua área de atuação, para atender as funções de natureza estratégica,

tecnológica, ambiental e de sustentabilidade, requeridas na geração de novos

conhecimentos e nos processos de produção e serviços.

Esse profissional pode:

• atuar em organizações públicas, privadas ou do terceiro setor, em especial

na área de Ciência e Tecnologia (C&T), como pesquisador, gestor e consultor;

• atuar em atividades de pesquisa em Ciência e Tecnologia, inclusive por

meio de estudos em nível de pós-graduação stricto sensu e/ou lato sensu;

• atuar no comércio (vendas, gerenciamento e serviços relacionados a

produtos na área de C&T ou em outras áreas que exijam as competências e

habilidades de um profissional formado em nível superior);

A ideia de implantar uma formação em ciclos nas universidades brasileiras

surge em um contexto marcado pela expansão das matrículas na educação

superior. A formação em ciclos incentivada pelo Programa de Reestruturação e

Expansão das Universidades Federais Brasileiras do MEC induz as IFES a

realizarem reestruturações da arquitetura acadêmica a fim de melhorar o

processo formativo na graduação .

alteração da arquitetura curricular em nível de graduação já estava inicia da, a

partir do Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia da UFABC.

Inspirada na organização da formação superior proposta por Anísio

Teixeira para a concepção da Universidade de Brasília, no início da década de

1960, no Processo de Bolonha e nos colleges estadunidenses, mas incorporando

um desenho inovador necessário para responder às nossas próprias e atuais

d emandas de formação acadêmica, a proposta de implantação dos Bacharelados

Interdisciplinares pela UFABC foi pioneira 1 .

O modelo tradicional de um a graduação com itinerários de formação

exposto a conhecimentos na fronteira da pesquisa científica e tecnológica) e na

formação co ntinuada, incentivada pela constante mudança do perfil do Bacharel 5 .

A estrutura do BC&T é constituída por três grupos de disciplinas, que

devem perfazer no mínimo 190 créditos , adicionadas de 120 horas de

atividades complementares extracurriculares, totalizando 2.400 horas . Cada

crédito equivale a 12 horas de aula, teórica e/ou prática (em laboratório). Os

componentes curriculares são oferecidos em ciclos quadrimestrais. Sua carga

As disciplinas do Bacharelado em Ciência e Tecnologia estão dividas pelas

seguintes categorias:

Disciplinas obrigatórias : pertencentes a um grupo de disciplinas que

devem necessariamente ser cursadas com aprovação para a integralização do

curso. No caso do BC&T, o aluno deve cursar 90 créditos em disciplinas desta

categoria determinadas neste projeto pedagógico.

Disciplinas de opção-limitada : presentes em um grupo selecionado de

disciplinas, com sugestões estabelecidas neste projeto pedagógico, que

permitem ao aluno aprofundar seus conhecimentos em determinadas áreas do

conhecimento, fazendo relações interdisciplinares com os conhecimentos

ofertados pelas disciplinas obrigatórias. Tais disciplinas ainda não apresentam

caráter profissionalizante específico , mas já direcionam a formação do aluno

para determinada área. No BC&T, o aluno deve cursar um mínimo de 57

créditos em disciplinas dessa categoria.
